All 14 queries ran and gave plausible answers. I checked T11, T12 and T13 by hand, and the other outputs against the data I could see. I didn't separately check T6's tie-breaking, because the output had no ties. A few notes on how the queries are written:
- Queries over a file that start with `/` begin with `| ` to avoid the Git Bash path conversion.
- T3, T7 and T10 answer with keyword keys such as `:db`. The task asks for an object, and the JSON output printed them as plain strings.
- T8 and T13 convert the keyword keys back to strings with `keyword`.

T1: | /data/users | filter ~(/active) | filter ~(at :email | coalesce "" | lower | endsWith "@example.com") | count
T2: | /data/users | filter ~(/roles | any ~(lower | eq "admin")) | sort ~(/name | lower) | * /name
T3: | /data/users | groupBy ~(at :profile | at :country | coalesce "unknown") * count
T4: | /data/users * (at :profile | at :age) | filter ~(ne null) | avg | round 2
T5: | filter ~(/state | eq "open") | * /labels | flat | * (/name | lower) | distinct | sort
T6: | sort ~([(/comments | desc) /number]) | take 3 * {:number /number :assignee (at :assignee | at :login)}
T7: | filter ~(/state | eq "open") | filter ~(at :assignee | ne null) | groupBy ~(/assignee/login) * count
T8: | unionOf /dependencies /devDependencies | entries | filter ~(/1 | startsWith "^") | sort ~(/0) | * ([(/0 | keyword) "@" /1] | join "")
T9: | /services | filter ~(at :enabled | eq true) | filter ~(/port | gt 8000) | * (/name | lower) | sort | join ","
T10: | lines | filter ~(split " " | /1 | eq "ERROR") | groupBy ~(split " " | /2) * count
T11: | lines | * (split " " | filter ~(startsWith "ms=")) | filter ~(count | gt 0) | * (/0 | drop 3 | parseJson) | avg | round 1
T12: | lines | drop 1 | filter ~(count | gt 0) * split "," | filter ~(/4 | ne "") | filter ~(/5 | lower | eq "shipped") | * (mulOf (/3 | parseJson) (/4 | parseJson)) | sum | round 2
T13: | lines | drop 1 | filter ~(count | gt 0) * split "," | filter ~(/4 | ne "") | filter ~(/5 | lower | ne "cancelled") | groupBy ~(/1) * (* (mulOf (/3 | parseJson) (/4 | parseJson)) | sum) | entries | * {:customer (/0 | keyword) :total (/1 | round 2)} | sort ~(/total | desc) | take 2
T14: | ["Banana" "apple" "Cherry" "banana" "fig" "APPLE" "date" "kiwi" "Fig" "elderberry"] * lower | distinct | sort ~([(count | desc) (/)]) | join "-"
